shared_elements: tall vertical stone slab/monolith as the support
frontal standing human figure occupying nearly the whole height
head with elaborate headdress or cap at the top
arms held in front across the chest/abdomen
circular disc or medallion ornament on the chest
carved bands/ornamental elements across the lower body (belt or skirt-like zone)
justification: Both are tall, symmetrical, front-facing monoliths carved with a single standing figure whose head and headdress fill the top, arms fold across the torso, and a round chest disc sits at centre — a genuinely comparable compositional scheme. They differ sharply in execution and density: A is a fine-line drawing of deeply undercut, horror-vacui relief crowded with masks and scrolls, whereas B is a weathered stone with sparse, shallow incised outlines and large blank surfaces, and the media of presentation (engraved illustration vs. museum photograph) further separate them.
